newsitem.title: USA: US FERC voids Illinois pipeline company's practice.
newsitem.headline: US FERC voids Illinois pipeline company's practice.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday barred a number of contracting practices of the Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America, a subsidiary of Occidental Petroleum Corp, and sternly rebuked the company.

After a July technical hearing on the Illinois-based company's pricing practices, the commission said it determined that Natural restricted capacity release rights by rescinding discounted rates when firm shippers released capacity.
The commission said Natural also reserved the right to terminate firm service on 24 hours' notice, and required shippers to sign non-disclosure agreements.
It said such terms and conditions of service deviated from Natural's service agreement, but there was no filing with FERC as is required for material deviations.

"In sum, to me the picture is one of exercise of market power in contravention of our regulatory scope. We will not tolerate or condone such practices whether by Natural or anyone else," FERC Chairman Elizabeth Moler said.
The commission order said Natural's exerise of a unilateral right to cancel firm service made it a "semi-firm" service that was not in the company's filed tariff.
The commission ordered Natural to file agreements and contracts with it that deviate from its filed contracts.
